definitionEn: the act or ceremony of putting a dead person's body into a grave
situation: Talking about how and where a dead person's body is placed in the ground, often during a ceremony.

examples.text: My grandfather didn't want to be cremated; he asked for a simple [[burial]] beside his wife.
The soldier's remains were finally brought home for [[burial]] eighty years after the war.
Hundreds of fans waited outside the cemetery gates during the private [[burial]] of the singer.

texts: Archaeologists have found an ancient royal [[burial]] site under a car park.
Some religions require [[burial]] within a day of death.
The council now charges over two thousand pounds for a [[burial]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Похоронный марш — funeral march. Burial — само погребение, а церемония, процессия и музыка — это funeral.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Burial ground — место древних захоронений. Funeral — церемония, а graveyard и cemetery сами значат «кладбище», слово ground к ним не добавляют.

nuance.text: After the church service, only close family went to the cemetery for the [[burial]].
nuance.explanationRu: Funeral — вся церемония прощания, со службой и речами. Burial — сам момент погребения. Служба уже прошла, на кладбище остаётся только burial.

reverse.text: She was cremated after a small [[funeral]] attended by close friends.
reverse.explanationRu: Кремация исключает погребение в землю, поэтому burial здесь невозможно. Funeral — похороны как церемония, при любом обряде.

fixIt.text: Because of their religious beliefs, the family chose [[funeral]] rather than cremation.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кремации противопоставляют burial — погребение в землю. Funeral — похороны вообще, они бывают и при кремации.

wordFormation.text: The exact place of her [[burial]] remained a family secret for decades.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Grandad died on Sunday. We're flying to Ireland for the funeral."
options: I'm so sorry. I hope the trip isn't too much of a burial for you.
I'm so sorry. Will the burial be in his home village?
Kindly inform me of the burial arrangements at your earliest convenience.
reply.explanationRu: Burial — погребение, вопрос о месте естественен. В первом ответе burial спутано с burden (тяжесть), третий звучит как деловое письмо, а не сочувствие другу.

definitionEn: to suddenly start crying, laughing, singing or burning
senseNote: Выбрано значение burst into tears / burst out laughing — «разразиться, вдруг начать», а не базовое «лопнуть».
situation: Someone hears news and, without any warning, starts crying or laughing loudly.

examples.text: When the doctor said the operation had gone well, his wife [[burst]] into tears.
The whole audience [[burst]] out laughing when the actor's fake moustache fell off.
Luckily nobody was hurt when the old van suddenly [[burst]] into flames on the motorway.

texts: The kids [[burst]] into song as soon as the school bus left.
She read his text and [[burst]] out laughing in the middle of the meeting.
The hall [[burst]] into applause when her name was announced.

badCollocation.noteRu: После burst into нужно существительное (tears, laughter), а после burst out — форма на -ing: burst out crying.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Внезапно расплакаться — burst into tears. Explode и fall с tears не сочетаются, а после start нужен глагол: start crying.

nuance.text: Reading her late mother's letters, she [[burst]] into tears.
nuance.explanationRu: Burst into tears — внезапно расплакаться. Start так не сочетается: можно started crying, но не started into tears.

reverse.text: She [[started]] crying quietly so that nobody would notice.
reverse.explanationRu: Тихо и незаметно — это started crying. Burst значит внезапно и бурно, и после него нужно into tears или out crying.

fixIt.text: When the teacher's chair suddenly collapsed, the children [[exploded]] out laughing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Разразиться смехом — burst out laughing. Explode out laughing так не говорят; с explode возможно только explode with laughter.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did your sister react when she got into medical school?"
options: She burst into a calm, polite smile and said thank you.
She burst into crying, and then she burst into laughing.
She burst into tears — happy ones, luckily!
reply.explanationRu: Burst into tears — бурно расплакаться, это естественный ответ. Спокойная улыбка с burst не сочетается, а burst into crying — ошибка: нужно burst into tears или burst out crying.

rewrite.original: When she heard the joke, she suddenly started laughing loudly.
rewrite.frame: When she heard the joke, she ____ laughing.

definitionEn: to avoid a usual rule, process or person in order to act faster
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «обходить правила, процедуру или начальство», а не «объезжать город».
situation: Someone skips the official procedure or goes over their manager's head to get something done quickly.

examples.text: To save time, she [[bypassed]] her line manager and emailed the director directly.
Hackers found a way to [[bypass]] the bank's security checks and access customer accounts.
Patients who can pay privately can often [[bypass]] the long waiting lists for surgery.

texts: You can't just [[bypass]] the approval process because you're in a hurry.
Some apps let children [[bypass]] age checks far too easily.
Good leaders don't [[bypass]] their team when making big decisions.

badCollocation.noteRu: Обойти лужу или человека на улице — walk around или step around. Bypass — про дороги, правила и процедуры.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальный порядок в организации — channels: go through или bypass the usual channels. Canals — водные каналы, pipes — трубы, streams — ручьи.

nuance.text: To test the airport, an undercover reporter [[bypassed]] security by walking in through a staff entrance.
nuance.explanationRu: Pass security — пройти досмотр как положено. Bypass — обойти его стороной. Через служебный вход досмотр не проходят, а обходят.

reverse.text: All passengers must [[pass]] through security before boarding.
reverse.explanationRu: Пройти через досмотр — pass through security. Bypass значило бы, что пассажиры обходят досмотр, а это противоположный смысл.

fixIt.text: The manager [[overtook]] the normal approval process and signed the contract himself.
fixIt.explanationRu: Overtake — обогнать (машину, конкурента). Действовать в обход процедуры — bypass.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager says: "IT approval takes three weeks, but we need the new software by Friday."
options: Could we bypass the usual approval just this once and let IT check it later?
Great, then let's bypass Friday and install it on Thursday.
Whatever, just bypass the lot, mate, nobody cares.
reply.explanationRu: Bypass — обойти процедуру, поэтому естественно предложить обойти согласование. «Bypass Friday» бессмысленно, а третий ответ слишком грубый для совещания.

rewrite.original: She went straight to the CEO without talking to her manager first.
rewrite.frame: She ____ her manager and went straight to the CEO.

definitionEn: the group of senior ministers who make the main decisions in a government
senseNote: Выбрано значение «кабинет министров», а не «шкаф»; кабинет начальника по-английски — office.
situation: The prime minister meets the most senior ministers to agree on important government decisions.

examples.text: The [[cabinet]] meets every Tuesday morning to discuss government policy.
After winning the election, she gave three women key jobs in her new [[cabinet]].
My brother follows politics closely and can name every minister in the [[cabinet]].

texts: She was the youngest woman ever to sit in the [[cabinet]].
The [[cabinet]] approved the plan after a long debate.
He was sacked from the [[cabinet]] for leaking secret documents.

badCollocation.noteRu: Кабинет директора — the director's office. Cabinet — это кабинет министров или шкаф, но не комната.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перестановки в правительстве — a cabinet reshuffle (буквально «перетасовка»). Rotation, remix и reshaping в этом сочетании не употребляются.

nuance.text: The president has chosen a new [[cabinet]], with women in half of the top jobs.
nuance.explanationRu: Cabinet — кабинет министров, то есть группа людей. Office — комната или учреждение; назначить туда министров на половину постов нельзя.

reverse.text: Could you come to my [[office]] after lunch? We need to talk.
reverse.explanationRu: Кабинет как комната — office. Cabinet — правительство или шкаф, туда не приходят поговорить.

fixIt.text: The new prime minister will present her [[office]] of ministers to parliament on Monday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кабинет министров — cabinet (of ministers). Office — кабинет-комната, к правительству это слово не относится.

reply.context: A British colleague says: "Big news — the prime minister has just sacked half the cabinet!"
options: Really? Did they move the cabinet into a bigger kitchen?
Really? Who's going to join the new cabinet, then?
Indeed? One trusts the cabinet shall be reconstituted forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Cabinet здесь — кабинет министров, поэтому уместно спросить о новых министрах. Первый ответ путает его со шкафом, третий звучит архаично и чопорно.

definitionEn: careful planning to get what you want, often without caring about others
senseNote: Выбрано значение «холодный расчёт, расчётливость», а не математическое вычисление.
situation: Someone acts kindly or makes a choice only because they expect to gain something from it.

examples.text: Critics said the minister's visit to the flooded town was cold [[calculation]], not real concern.
Her friendliness towards the new boss was pure [[calculation]]: she wanted the promotion.
The decision to raise prices was based on the [[calculation]] that loyal customers would not leave.

texts: Was it love or [[calculation]] that made her marry him?
Politicians rarely admit that [[calculation]] guides their choices.
His generosity was never entirely free of [[calculation]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Брак по расчёту — a marriage of convenience. Calculation в этом выражении не используют.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Холодный расчёт — cold calculation. Counting, computing и estimation — про подсчёт и вычисления, а не про расчётливость в поступках.

nuance.text: His apology sounded less like real regret and more like cold [[calculation]].
nuance.explanationRu: Calculation может значить корыстный расчёт в поступках людей. Computation — только вычисления (в математике, у компьютеров), о мотивах человека так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Her sudden kindness to her rich old aunt was pure [[prudence]]: she hoped to inherit the house.
fixIt.explanationRu: Prudence — благоразумие, это похвала. Корыстный расчёт — calculation.

wordFormation.text: Everyone could see that his tears on the talk show were a matter of [[calculation]], not feeling.

reply.context: A friend says: "Tom only started visiting his grandmother after he heard about her will."
options: Sounds like pure calculation to me. Poor woman!
Wow, his calculation must be excellent. Was he good at maths?
One discerns a certain degree of calculation in his conduct, I'm afraid.
reply.explanationRu: Calculation — корыстный расчёт, первый ответ точно передаёт мысль. Второй путает его с вычислениями, третий слишком книжный для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: She only married him because she wanted his money.
rewrite.frame: Her marriage was a matter of ____, not love.

definitionEn: a piece of strong cloth used for oil painting, or a painting done on it
senseNote: Выбрано значение «холст, полотно (картина)»; значение «брезент, парусина» не рассматриваем.
situation: An artist prepares the surface for an oil painting, or a gallery shows several large paintings.

examples.text: She stretched a new [[canvas]] over the wooden frame and started sketching.
An unknown buyer paid two million pounds for a small [[canvas]] by a little-known Dutch painter.
The gallery's largest [[canvas]] is six metres wide and took the artist three years to paint.

texts: The paint had cracked, so the [[canvas]] needed careful repair.
He prefers painting on [[canvas]] rather than on wood.
Each [[canvas]] in the show depicts the same lighthouse at a different hour.

badCollocation.noteRu: По-русски картину «пишут», а по-английски — paint: paint a canvas, paint a picture.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Натянуть холст на подрамник — stretch a canvas. Extend и lengthen — «удлинить, продлить», draw — «рисовать»; с canvas так не говорят.

nuance.text: Before starting, the artist covered the whole [[canvas]] with a thin layer of grey paint.
nuance.explanationRu: До начала работы картины ещё нет — есть только холст, canvas. Picture — уже готовое изображение.

reverse.text: The children drew a [[picture]] of their house with crayons.
reverse.explanationRu: Детский рисунок карандашами — picture. Canvas — холст для живописи маслом или картина на нём.

fixIt.text: The gallery has just bought a huge [[cloth]] by a young Italian painter.
fixIt.explanationRu: Картину-полотно по-английски называют canvas. Cloth — ткань вообще, о картине так не говорят.

reply.context: At an art fair, a friend points at a huge oil painting: "Can you imagine that on our living-room wall?"
options: Only if we paint the wall with canvas first.
The canvas is, I must respectfully submit, of excessive dimensions.
It's a gorgeous canvas, but it's twice the size of our wall!
reply.explanationRu: Canvas — картина на холсте, третий ответ естественный. Первый делает из canvas краску, второй звучит как официальный доклад, а не разговор с другом.

definitionEn: the power or practical ability of a person, machine or organisation to do something
senseNote: Чаще всего о технике, организациях и странах: the capabilities of a system, military capability.
situation: Describing what a new phone, a company or a country's army is really able to do.

examples.text: For such a cheap phone, it has impressive night-vision [[capabilities]].
Opening offices in Asia is beyond the company's current [[capabilities]].
The lab now has the [[capability]] to sequence a full genome in a single day.

texts: The project will test the team's [[capabilities]] to the limit.
Few people use all the [[capabilities]] of their smartphones.
The hospital is expanding its research [[capabilities]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Способности к музыке или языкам — a talent / a gift for. Capability — возможности системы, организации или человека выполнить задачу.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Nuclear capability — способность страны создать ядерное оружие. Possibility и opportunity — «вероятность» и «шанс», talent — природный дар; с nuclear так не говорят.

nuance.text: The main selling point of the new watch is its sleep-tracking [[capability]].
nuance.explanationRu: Capability — что устройство умеет делать (следить за сном). Capacity — объём или вместимость (память, зал), к функциям часов это не подходит.

reverse.text: The new stadium has a [[capacity]] of sixty thousand people.
reverse.explanationRu: Вместимость стадиона — capacity. Capability — возможности и умения, а не число мест.

fixIt.text: My old laptop doesn't have the [[possibility]] to run modern video games.
fixIt.explanationRu: Possibility — вероятность, шанс. О том, что умеет техника, говорят capability: doesn't have the capability to.

wordFormation.text: Few experts doubt the country's [[capability]] to build its own satellites.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Can our current website handle online payments, or do we need a new one?"
options: Its capability is about twenty gigabytes, so we're fine.
It doesn't have that capability yet, but a plug-in could add it.
Please be advised that a capability assessment will be conducted in due course.
reply.explanationRu: Capability — умение системы что-то делать, второй ответ точный. В первом capability спутано с capacity (объём), третий — канцелярская отписка, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: The company is not able to deliver so many orders in one week.
rewrite.frame: Delivering so many orders in one week is beyond the company's ____.

definitionEn: an economic system in which businesses are privately owned and run for profit
situation: Discussing an economy where private companies, not the state, own most businesses and compete for profit.

examples.text: After 1991, many Eastern European countries switched from central planning to [[capitalism]].
Supporters of [[capitalism]] say that competition drives innovation and keeps prices low.
The film is a dark satire of [[capitalism]], set in a company where workers are ranked by profit.

texts: The course looks at how [[capitalism]] developed in eighteenth-century Britain.
Even its critics admit that [[capitalism]] has created enormous wealth.
Is modern [[capitalism]] compatible with protecting the planet?

badCollocation.noteRu: Перед существительным нужно прилагательное: a capitalist country, a capitalist economy. Capitalism — название самой системы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Экономическая система — capitalism (free-market capitalism). Capital — деньги, капитал; capitalization — рыночная стоимость компании; profitability — прибыльность.

nuance.text: Under [[capitalism]], most shops and factories belong to private owners.
nuance.explanationRu: Capitalism — экономическая система: «при капитализме». Capital — деньги или имущество для бизнеса (или столица), «при капитале» не живут.

reverse.text: The start-up needs more [[capital]] to hire new engineers.
reverse.explanationRu: Деньги для развития бизнеса — capital. Capitalism — система, её нельзя привлечь или потратить.

fixIt.text: In the 1990s the country moved from a planned economy to free-market [[capitalist]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно название системы — существительное capitalism. Capitalist — «капиталист» или прилагательное «капиталистический».

wordFormation.text: Students on the course compare [[capitalism]] with other economic systems.

reply.context: In a seminar, the tutor asks: "What do you see as the main strength of a market economy?"
options: I'd say capitalism is good at encouraging innovation, though it can increase inequality.
I'd say capitalism, because the capital city usually has the best jobs.
Capitalism totally rocks, dude. Money, money, money!
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ корректно использует capitalism и звучит взвешенно. Во втором capitalism спутано со столицей (capital city), третий слишком развязный для семинара.

definitionEn: based on or supporting an economy of private business and profit
situation: Describing a country, economy or society where private companies compete and make profits for their owners.

examples.text: In a [[capitalist]] economy, most businesses are owned by private individuals rather than the state.
The novel shows the dark side of [[capitalist]] society through the eyes of a delivery driver.
The country's rapid shift to a [[capitalist]] system created a new class of very rich businessmen.

texts: The magazine is openly critical of the [[capitalist]] system.
Advertising lies at the heart of [[capitalist]] culture.
The two countries had very different economies: one [[capitalist]], the other communist.

badCollocation.noteRu: Капиталовложения — capital investment. Capitalist значит «капиталистический» (о системе, обществе, стране), а не «капитальный».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед system нужно прилагательное capitalist. Capitalism — существительное, capital — капитал или столица, capitalized — «написанный с заглавной буквы».

nuance.text: Most [[capitalist]] countries still provide free schooling for all children.
nuance.explanationRu: Capitalist описывает экономическую систему страны в целом. Commercial — «коммерческий», о бизнесе, товарах и прибыли; страну так не называют.

reverse.text: Despite bad reviews, the film was a huge [[commercial]] success.
reverse.explanationRu: Коммерческий успех фильма — commercial success. Capitalist описывает систему, а не прибыльность отдельного проекта.

fixIt.text: In a [[capitalism]] economy, prices are set mainly by supply and demand.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед economy нужно прилагательное capitalist. Capitalism — существительное, название системы.

definitionEn: the goods that a ship, plane or truck carries
situation: Talking about the goods loaded onto a ship or plane and transported to another country.

examples.text: The ship was carrying a [[cargo]] of frozen fish when it ran aground off the coast.
Most of the airline's profits now come from [[cargo]], not passengers.
Dock workers spent the whole night unloading the [[cargo]] from the container ship.

texts: Customs officers searched the [[cargo]] for hidden drugs.
A [[cargo]] ship blocked the canal for six days.
The truck lost part of its [[cargo]] on the motorway.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Груз ответственности» — the burden of responsibility. Cargo — только настоящий груз на корабле, самолёте или грузовике.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Грузовое судно — a cargo ship. Load — груз в кузове или нагрузка, weight — вес, burden — тяжкое бремя; со ship они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The plane carries both passengers and [[cargo]], such as mail and fresh flowers.
nuance.explanationRu: Cargo — коммерческий груз: почта, товары, цветы. Luggage — личные вещи пассажиров (чемоданы, сумки), почта к ним не относится.

reverse.text: Please don't leave your [[luggage]] unattended anywhere in the station.
reverse.explanationRu: Чемоданы и сумки пассажиров — luggage. Cargo — груз для перевозки, а не личные вещи.

fixIt.text: The plane was carrying forty tonnes of [[load]], mostly medicine and food.
fixIt.explanationRu: Груз самолёта или судна — cargo. Load — «груз, нагрузка» в общем смысле и обычно исчисляемое: a load of.

reply.context: Your friend, who works at the port, texts: "Can't meet tonight, sorry. A ship came in late."
options: No worries. Is the cargo coming to dinner with us instead?
Acknowledged. Kindly confirm the cargo discharge schedule.
No worries. Are you stuck unloading cargo all night?
reply.explanationRu: Cargo — груз с судна, третий ответ естественный. Первый говорит о грузе как о человеке, второй звучит как служебная записка, а не сообщение другу.
